title: Infrastructure Weekly Update - 2026-09-14
content:
Weekly summary (2026-09-08 -> 2026-09-14)

High level:
- Fleet availability remained >= 99.3% across all hosted regions; small degradation in us-west-2 on 9/11 during a rolling kernel update (see incident below).
- Continued H100 ramp: 240 H100 cards now live (up from 160 last week). A100 decomm schedule started for older reserve pools.
- Capacity planning update: steady demand growth (~12% w/w for large-gen workloads). We recommend increasing reserved capacity in eu-west-1 and ap-south-1 for Q4.

Key metrics (last 7d):
- Average GPU utilization (hosted pools): 63% (target 60-70%)
- Peak queue latency (99th percentile scheduling delay): 820ms (goal < 600ms) - driven by afternoon US spikes
- Median model start time (cold): 580ms; warm starts: 120ms
- Pre-warmed pool hit-rate: 72% (up from 65% last week)
- On-demand cost per token (estimated): stable, but H100 spot price fluctuations increased margin variability

Highlights and progress:
1) H100 migration
- Completed validation for H100 driver stack across serving-runtime v2.3.2. All benchmark suites passed for the 8k sequence tests.
- Canary workload started for two high-throughput customers on h100-large pools (JIRA-7890). No regressions in latency or QA eval scores so far.
- Remaining work: finalize perf knobs for kernel selection at batch sizes >48 (Marcus + Lina). Timeline: perf knobs merged by 9/20, rollout to non-prod by 9/21.

2) Regional capacity & new region onboarding
- eu-west-1: Request to increase reserved H100 capacity by 2 racks (approx +96 GPUs) for Oct launch. Product sign-off scheduled 9/16.
- ap-south-1: early partner demand - proposing a small reserved pool (24 GPUs) and larger on-demand burst; awaiting cost estimate from cloud procurement (Priya).
- us-west-2: investigating persistent afternoon queuing - hypothesis is localized bursty traffic from two enterprise customers. We set temporary per-customer throttles and saw a 30% reduction in tail queue latency.

3) Autoscaling and pre-warming improvements
- Autoscaler V1.4 deployed to prod can scale GPU pools 2x faster (shorter cool-downs + predictive ramp). Initial A/B test (10% of traffic) shows 18% fewer cold starts.
- Pre-warm heuristics adjusted to bias toward models with rising recent traffic; pilot increased hit-rate to 72%. Need to tune eviction policy to maintain memory headroom during multi-tenant bursts.

4) Cost and reservations
- Finance requests: scenario plan for Q4 committed capacity. Baseline demand growth (~12% w/w) suggests 20% reserved capacity increase to avoid on-demand premium.
- Action: Priya to run 3 reservation scenarios (conservative, base, aggressive) and share by 9/18 (JIRA-7921).

Incidents & oncall notes:
- 2026-09-11 02:15 UTC: Rolling kernel update in us-west-2 caused increased pod eviction rate for ~45m leading to a transient <5% drop in availability for hosted API. Root cause: a vendor kernel edge-case with our nvlink config on a sub-set of A100 hosts. Rollback to previous kernel resolved immediate impact. Long-term fix: vendor patch + validation; scheduled for 9/22. Postmortem assigned to Ethan.
- 2026-09-12 18:40 UTC: Higher than expected job preemption in burst pools - caused by misconfigured spot fallback policy; fixed in-place. Follow-up: add unit test to catch policy regressions.

Open risks / concerns:
- If H100 spot volatility continues through October, unit economics for spike workloads may degrade - we need options for blended fleet pricing or more aggressive reservation for critical customers.
- Queue latency tail still above SLO during US peak hours; short-term mitigations (per-customer throttles) are working but this is brittle. Need better global routing to shift non-latency-sensitive workloads to lower-cost regions.
- ap-south-1 onboarding has incomplete capacity planning for networking (EFA / RDMA) - missing cloud provider confirmation on bandwidth guarantees.

Work items and owners (next 2 weeks):
- Finalize H100 perf knobs and merge (Marcus, Lina) - due 2026-09-20
- Reservation scenarios for Q4 (Priya) - due 2026-09-18 (JIRA-7921)
- eu-west-1 reserve approval follow-up & cost sign-off (Asha + Product) - meeting 2026-09-16
- Kernel vendor patch validation & rollback plan (Ethan) - patch scheduled 2026-09-22
- Autoscaler eviction policy tuning & memory headroom tests (SRE + infra) - target 2026-09-28
- Global routing experiment: shift batch reranking workloads to eu-west-1 during US peaks (Solutions Eng + Product) - pilot 2026-09-25

Meeting notes (this week):
- 9/10 Infra Sync (attendees: Asha, Ethan, Lina, Marcus, Priya, Zoe (SRE))
  - Discussed H100 canary metrics; agreed threshold for rollback is +10% tail latency or >=2 customer regressions.
  - Priya to coordinate reservation scenarios with finance.
  - Zoe raised SRE concern about eviction policy; agreed to run chaos test next week.

- 9/12 Capacity Planning (attendees: Product infra reps, Asha, Priya)
  - Product requested guaranteed capacity for two EU customers for Oct promotions - need 96 GPUs in eu-west-1. Procurement needs final approval by 9/16.

Decisions made:
- Start decommissioning the oldest A100 reserve pool (pool-id: reserve-a100-2022-03) on 2026-10-05. Replacement plan: staggered migration to H100 + a small transitional A40 pool for low-priority workloads.
- Approve autoscaler roll-forward; will monitor 2-week window before global rollout.

Notes to self / open questions:
- Confirm whether vendor patch for kernel impacts any H100 hosts (vendor says no but need independent validation).
- Do we want to prioritize expanding pre-warm capacity over reservations for ap-south-1? Tradeoff: short-term lat improvements vs long-term unit cost.

Attachments / links referenced:
- H100 perf benchmark logs: https://artifacts.internal.redwood/h100-bench/2026-09-10
- Postmortem (kernel rollback): CONFLUENCE-INC-2026-09-11
- Reservation scenarios (WIP): JIRA-7921

Bottom line recommendations:
- Approve incremental eu-west-1 reservation (+96 GPUs) conditional on product sign-off 9/16. This avoids expensive on-demand spikes for scheduled promotions.
- Continue H100 rollout but keep the canary narrow until perf knobs merge.
- Fast-follow SRE eviction-policy tuning and kernel vendor patch validation to reduce tail queue risk.

Action items for next update:
- Priya: Q4 reservation scenarios (due 9/18)
- Marcus & Lina: H100 perf knobs merged + non-prod rollout (due 9/21)
- Ethan: Postmortem draft for 9/11 incident (due 9/17)
- SRE: Chaos test plan for eviction policy (share by 9/20)

Quick informal notes (scratchpad):
- saw two enterprise customers with burst patterns 14:00-16:00 PDT; talk to CSMs to smooth schedulers?
- consider short-term customer-specific burst rules vs global QoS

--
Document draft created during Thurs infra sync. Will update after reservation meeting on 9/16 and kernel patch validation on 9/22.
